report.source_text: On contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) scan, no contrast opacification was noted in the middle and left hepatic veins and partial opacification was noted in the right hepatic vein suggestive of complete thrombosis of middle and left hepatic veins and partial thrombosis of the right hepatic vein associated with slit-like visualization of the hepatic part of IVC. A slight enlargement of the caudate lobe was noted. The liver shows a heterogeneous mottled appearance (nutmeg liver) (Figure 3).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 40-year-old woman presented with one month of abdominal pain, vomiting, abdominal tenderness and hepatomegaly. Initial grayscale ultrasound revealed heterogeneous liver echotexture, a fibrous cord replacing the middle hepatic vein, and mild ascites. Doppler ultrasound showed absent hepatic vein flow confirming hepatic vein obstruction. Contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated thrombosis of the middle and left hepatic veins and partial thrombosis of the right hepatic vein with caudate lobe enlargement and nutmeg liver appearance consistent with Budd Chiari syndrome. She subsequently underwent successful hepatic vein stenting via the right internal jugular vein.
